author: Sam Tiahnybik
title: Company Overview Network-1 Technologies (“NTIP”, “Network-1”
text:
Company Overview Network-1 Technologies' ((NYSEMKT: NTIP ), "Network-1" or the "Company") primary business is the development, licensing, and protection of its intellectual property (IP). It currently owns 50 patents including the Remote Power Patent, the Mirror Worlds Patent Portfolio, the Cox Patent Portfolio, the QoS patents, and the Nix patents. The Company continually reviews opportunities to acquire or license additional intellectual property. The Company's strategy is to pursue licensing opportunities with respect to its intellectual property. Furthermore, the Company works with inventors and patent owners to assist in the development and monetization of its patented technologies. The Company was founded in 1990 and is headquartered in New York City.
Investment Thesis The Company has a strong balance sheet with $52.3mn in cash and no debt. Recent settlements with Avaya ( OTCQX:AVYA ) and Juniper (NYSE: JNPR ) should add nearly $16mn to the cash balance. The Company has a strong history of defending its IP portfolio against tech giants such as Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) and Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT ). Pending litigation against YouTube, Google (NASDAQ: GOOG ), and Facebook (NASDAQ: FB ) could represent millions in upside. The Company has significant insider ownership, all officers and directors owning ~31% of the shares outstanding. Past Litigation: The Company has successfully defended its IP portfolio against some of the biggest players in the technological world including Apple, Microsoft, and Cisco (NASDAQ: CSCO ). Litigation with Apple and Microsoft commenced in 2013 in relation to U.S. Patent No. 6,006,227, a patent within the Company's Mirror Worlds Patent Portfolio. In 2015 and 2016, both Apple and Microsoft settled their patent litigation with the Company paying Network-1 $25mn and $4.65mn respectively.
